target_customer: Korean consumers who hire local service providers (movers, tutors, planners) and the freelancers and small businesses who pay for leads
problem: Finding and comparing trustworthy local service providers in Korea was fragmented; providers needed a way to find new customers.
business_model: Marketplace where providers pay for customer quote requests and leads

founders.name: Robin Kim
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no background. A search summary named Hwan Kim as a founder; this is probably the same person under a Korean name but is unconfirmed, so not merged.

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided matching marketplace with quote requests and payments; mostly standard web and mobile engineering, with the difficulty in supply and demand balance.

defensibility.rationale: Provider supply and customer demand reinforced each other across 1,000+ service categories in one country, but local matching platforms are copyable and providers multi-home.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; a Korean private equity firm, Ark & Partners, took it private via a tender offer in 2024.

market_need_then: Soomgo launched in Korea around 2014 and 2015 as a horizontal marketplace for moving, lessons and events; no dated market size was found.

identity.logo: New logo, colors and slogan rolled out from 2025-03-06
identity.visual_style: Redesigned in 2025 to signal a broader life skills platform
identity.voice_and_tone: Slogan on the 2025 rebrand: life skills for a better everyday life.

rebrands.why: Marking ten years and a move from expert matching to a life skills platform, per Design Compass.

brand_strength.rationale: YC describes it as the number one local services marketplace in Korea and it ran a formal brand redesign at ten years, but no sources on mascot, community or brand driven growth were found.

outcome_analysis: Soomgo grew into the self described leading Korean local services marketplace with a 125 person team, raising a Series B in 2019 and nearly 30 million dollars in a Series C in June 2021 with total funding near 50 billion won. It was then bought out by Ark & Partners through a tender offer in 2024 at an undisclosed price, which looks like a private equity take private of a scaled business rather than a failure.
notes: Series B was 12.5 billion KRW (June 2019, per Platum and VentureSquare as summarized by search; USD not converted). Series C was 32 billion KRW, about 30 million dollars per KED Global. Unverified: a 2018 Series A (3.4M USD in ZoomInfo, listing on Seedtable), CB Insights total of 43M, and a 60M USD deal value; acquisition date conflicts (CB Insights 2024-05, other sources 2024-09 or 10). The company site returned 403. No dated 2017 competitor source found (Miso app listing and ahrefs keyword lists are undated), so the list is empty.
